To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mouse SRCL is a Lewisx receptor with a novel carbohydrate-recognition mechanism.

the interaction of mouse SRCL with Lewisx is based on a galactose-binding mechanism similar to that in the asialoglucoprotein receptor and that the conformation of human SRCL is different in crystals grown without calcium ions.
mouse SRCL binds Lewisx by a novel mechanism based on a primary site for galactose recognition and that the human receptor has the potential for endocytosis of its ligands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the scavenger receptor C type lectin (SR-CLEC) and how it recognizes the Lewisx trimeric carbohydrate.
the molecular mechanisms of the scavenger receptor C-lectin (SRCL), which is unique in the group of class A scavengers.
the structure, function, and mechanism of action of the human scavenger receptor class A member 2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mouse SRCL binds Lewisx by a novel mechanism that is distinct from the mechanism by which selectins and DC- SIGN interact with related glycans.
mouse SRCL is a novel type of galactose-binding protein that recognizes the Lewisx trimeric carbohydrate.
mouse and human SRCL bind to the Lewisx triscaccharide by a unique mechanism that is distinct from other known lectin-glycan interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interaction between mouse SRLC and Lewisx is based on a galactose-binding motif that is similar to the binding sites in the asialogycoprotein receptor and in the selectins, and that this interaction is the basis for the specificity of mouse SRCL for the Lewisx glycan.
we have identified the basis for the high selectivity of mouse SRCL for Lewisx and that we have shown the basis for the specificity of a novel mechanism for galactose binding in a lectin.

the SRCL binds to the Lewisx trimer through a novel mechanism involving a galactose-binding motif, which is similar to that found in other C-type lectins, but with a different orientation and a different mode of calcium coordination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CRD of SRCL is not a typical C-type lectin.
the SRCL CRD is a novel type of carbohydrate-recognition domain with a primary galactoside-binding site that is distinct from the lectin-like domains of selectins and DC- SIGN.
the SRCL CRD is a novel type of lectin that binds to a specific trisaccharidic ligand by a novel mechanism.
